headline: The US Medicare and Medicaid agency plans to publish the results of an AI pilot that flags Medicaid fraud before payment and hopes to suspend far more suspect providers.
score_reason: Pool 6, lowered to 5: the remarks were made on 15 Oct, before the window; savings figures are CMS's own and the pilot results are not yet published.
importance_line: Providers who could be barred from federal programmes and taxpayers whose money is at stake are affected first, then states and the agency itself, but the pilot's results are not yet public, the savings figures are CMS's own, and Brandt admitted that “a lot of things” about WISeR, an AI-assisted pre-approval pilot for Medicare services, are not working.
summary: Nextgov/FCW reports that Kimberly Brandt, deputy administrator of the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS), the federal agency that runs both programmes, said at a conference in Santa Fe on Thursday 15 Oct 2026 that CMS will soon publish results of an Indiana pilot, run with the technology company Oracle, that uses AI to flag suspicious Medicaid billing before money is paid. She added that CMS is working with five more states on similar pilots and hopes provider suspensions will quadruple within six months, now that the Department of Health and Human Services has given CMS new power to bar providers from federal health programmes.
notes: Pool item was ExecutiveGov's relay of Nextgov/FCW (published 15 Oct, 22:38 GMT); the original was read and credited. Event date 15 Oct is before the window.
